title: The E3 ubiquitin ligase CRL4DDRM3 targets CDT1 for degradation to facilitate homologous recombination in Arabidopsis
content:
Abstract
DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are considered the most cytotoxic form of DNA damage. Homologous recombination (HR) is an accurate DSB repair pathway. However, the regulatory mechanisms of HR are still poorly understood in plants. The DNA replication licensing factor CDC10-dependent transcript 1 (CDT1) is highly conserved in eukaryotes. The human CDT1 is subjected to polyubiquitination and degradation mediated by the E3 ubiquitin ligases CRL4CDT2 and SCFSKP2, ensuring that DNA replicates only once per cell cycle. But the E3 ubiquitin ligase(s) targeting plant CDT1 have not been firmly identified yet. Here we show that a previously uncharacterized WD40 protein, DNA Damage Response Mutant 3 (DDRM3)/Hypersensitive to Zebularine 11 (HZE11), facilitates HR in Arabidopsis. The ddrm3 mutants show reduced HR efficiency and are thus hypersensitive to multiple DSB-inducing agents. Biochemical analysis reveals that DDRM3 directly interacts with DDB1 to form the E3 ubiquitin ligase CRL4DDRM3, which mediates the polyubiquitination and degradation of CDT1. Genetically, silencing CDT1 partially rescues the hypersensitivity of ddrm3 to DSB-inducing agents. Interestingly, overexpression of CDT1 reduces HR efficiency. Altogether, these data suggest that DDRM3 facilitates HR by targeting CDT1 for degradation.
